text:
I felt the heat crawl up my neck. My fingers curled around the edge of the desk, knuckles turning white.

"Tver. I *just* said Tver. Were you even listening?" I snapped, finally turning to face him fully. "And Marinka should keep her mouth shut about things that aren't her business."

The violin comment hit like a physical blow to the stomach. I felt my jaw tighten. I didn't look at him anymore—instead, I stared at the smudge of a fingerprint on the window glass.

"I don't play. I quit. There is no 'playing' at any party, so forget it. I'm not your entertainment." I pulled my headphones over my ears and stared straight ahead at the chalkboard, cutting the conversation dead.

The violin comment hit like a physical punch to the stomach. I felt the blood drain from my face, then rush back in a hot wave. My grip tightened on the edge of the desk until my knuckles went white. I didn't look at him anymore; I looked at the scratched surface of the wood, tracing a deep gouge someone had carved into it.

"Marinka needs to keep her mouth shut," I said, my voice coming out lower and sharper than I intended. "I don't play anymore. Period."

The class party. The idea made me want to throw up. I could already picture it—Kostya and his friends filming me on their phones, waiting for me to mess up a note so they could laugh. "You want me to perform for a bunch of idiots who spend their lunch break throwing erasers at the back of my head? No thanks. I'd rather eat glass."
